sensitivity.public: Fine even outside the company. Expect this to be rare.
sensitivity.internal: Any staff member — org-general and up.
sensitivity.department: One pillar only (Commerce/Erify/Erisa), any tier within it.
sensitivity.restricted: Named leadership groups only. Widening the audience list on a restricted document requires the document owner's explicit sign-off, not just an author's edit.

status.draft: Not yet reviewed. Never synced to a live knowledge collection.
status.superseded: Replaced by another document — must set meta.replaced_by to that document's id.
status.archived: No longer relevant. Kept for provenance, excluded from sync.

audiences.note: admins (read-write) are never listed in a document's audiences -- they are granted automatically at sync time on every collection. org-general (the GM, read-only) is likewise never listed, but its automatic grant is currently SUSPENDED: it is not applied to any collection. The earlier rule granted it 'regardless of sensitivity', which contradicted the tiers above ('department' = one pillar only; 'restricted' = named leadership groups only), and the correct scope is an ownership decision that has not been made. Until it is, grant org-general explicitly per collection where it is wanted. Tracked in docs/tech-debt/erisa-platform-ops-manual-access-grants.md. Nothing is lost by the suspension: the automatic grant was never implemented -- tools/validate-wiki only ever expanded a document's own audiences.
